validity.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki flag assumes the mainline's 36-inch spec carries onto this Phase-1-expansion row, but LEAP's phased expansions (2023-2026) are NOT described as compression-only by DT Midstream's own materials, unlike the compression-station/capacity-expansion examples the protocol names elsewhere. DT Midstream's Aug 2023 investor presentation (https://s28.q4cdn.com/581450200/files/doc_presentations/2023/Aug/22/dtm-company-presentation-august-2023-vf.pdf, verified: contains 'LEAP', downloaded and read with pdftotext) states on its Phase-1-expansion slide: 'Project includes a combination of looping and compression' for the Phase 1-3 program, and lists 'LEAP pipeline looping' as a named key project update. Independently, Oil & Gas Journal (https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/55240028/dt-midstream-expanding-haynesville-marcellus-natural-gas-pipeline-systems, verified: contains 'DT Midstream' and 'looping') reports the same phased program uses 'incremental compression and looping.' A third independent source, DT Midstream's own FY2023 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1842022/000184202224000003/dtm-20231231.htm, verified: contains '209-mile') describes LEAP as a '209-mile lateral pipeline' as of Dec 31, 2023 (after Phase 1 and Phase 2 were placed in service) versus the ~150-155-mile figure trade press used before/during those phases and the system's current (2026) dtmidstream.com page describing a 221-mile system after Phase 4 — a real mileage increase consistent with new pipe (looping) having been added across the phase program, not compression alone. I could not find a Phase-1-specific mileage or diameter breakdown (DT Midstream's press releases on Phase 1 commissioning report only the capacity jump, 1.0->1.3 Bcf/d, matching this row's Capacity=300.00 MMcf/d, which does confirm this row is the correct Phase-1 match) or a Louisiana state permit record isolating Phase 1's construction scope, so I am not confident enough to assign 914 mm to this specific row without risking a fabricated per-phase attribute (standing rule 2). Marking this a concern rather than UNRESOLVED because the evidence actively contradicts the flag's implicit 'compression-only, blank is correct' resolution — a human needs to reconcile Length and Diameter together, not treat the blank as settled.
